svg.title: Convergence: stop review that never ends
svg.desc: Engraved plate on review convergence. A spiral closes in over round 1, round 2 and round 3 to the words reconsider the approach: after 3 rounds the reviewer stops listing and asks the author to reconsider the approach. The problem: one PR ran 50+ overnight review rounds, and about 59% of what was flagged had already been there on the first pass. Results reported at the source, before and after: PRs passing after one round, 65% to 78%; PRs needing 5+ rounds, 8.9% to 1.5%; mean reviews per PR, 2.08 to 1.32. These are the originating team’s numbers on their own repos. Source: A. Osmani, M. W. Lunt and Q. Wang, “How the Claude Code team does code review”, Anthropic, 15 October 2026, https://claude.dev/blog/solving-code-review-at-anthropic/. Independent implementation, not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic.
